listenings.text: Ladies and gentlemen, this is an announcement for passengers traveling to Tokyo on flight two four seven. The departure gate has changed from gate eleven to gate thirty-two, in the same terminal, and boarding will now begin at nine forty rather than nine twenty. Passengers with a connecting flight in Doha, please note that your layover is now under two hours, and staff at gate thirty-two will help you with the transfer. Passengers traveling with small children may board first. We apologize for the change and we thank you for your patience.

The advice everybody gives is to go off the beaten track, and almost nobody explains how. Here is the version that actually works. Do not look for the hidden gem, because the hidden gem is in every guide and it is packed by ten in the morning. Instead, pick one ordinary thing you do at home and do it there. Buy your bread. Go to a swimming pool. Sit in a park at five in the afternoon on a Tuesday. You will be surrounded by locals doing their Tuesday, not by visitors doing their holiday, and you will learn more about the place in an hour than in three days of landmarks. Only when you stop performing the trip does the trip start.

extra_audio.text: Ingrid says she saw Braulio at the harbour the day before, taking a photograph of the bicycles. He answers that he has never seen a city where everybody gets around on a bicycle. Ingrid tells him to wait until he sees Tokyo, and asks whether he is going. He says possibly next year, because his wife has been asking for ten years. Ingrid explains that she has been four times, and that both the food and the silence surprised her.
